claim_reviews.claim: English sense is “daytime” / time during the day.
Indonesian “siang hari” is a valid translation.
Malaysian “waktu siang” is a valid translation.
The answers are similar rather than strictly contrastive.

rationale: Both answers correctly express “daytime,” and the English cue is aligned. The forms overlap across Indonesian and Malaysian Malay, but the “similar” relation accurately avoids implying an exclusive national distinction.
